claim: Finding 7 ("A documented LinkedIn outbound funnel produced 2 paying clients from 487 connection requests in 30 days") is rated strength "Medium".
problem: The source is a single self-published founder blog post. The brief itself rates the other finding drawn from the same post (finding 8, the free-pilot economics) as "Low", and the role standard treats single-founder anecdotes as Low. Rating the same 30-day anecdote Medium overstates it, and the recommendations are built on it.
fix: Downgrade finding 7 to "Low" and say explicitly that the funnel is one founder's 30-day sample with no external verification (submit.co, which indexes the same post, likewise notes it hasn't checked founders' numbers).

claim: Recommendation 2: "roughly 100 targeted LinkedIn touches per held call, ~2 held calls per signed pilot, and about 1 paying client per 2 pilots. For 3 clients, plan ~300-500 targeted touches and 6+ pilots over 2-3 months".
problem: The arithmetic is inconsistent with the cited case and with its own per-unit rates. The source funnel is 487 connection requests to 8 held calls (~61 touches per held call, not ~100) and 487 requests to 2 paying clients. Walking the brief's own rates: 3 clients = 6 pilots = ~12 held calls = ~730 touches at 61 per call (or ~1,200 at its stated 100 per call). "300-500 touches" understates the documented effort by roughly 2x and is lower than the single case that produced only 2 clients.
fix: Restate as ~60-100 touches per held call, ~1 paying client per 2 pilots, and ~700-1,200 touches (roughly 500 per paying client) for 3 clients over 2-3 months; or drop the touch count and keep only the pilot/call ratios.

claim: Resources: Hinge buyer studies "with sample sizes stated (822 buyers/533 providers; 1,028 buyers; 1,914 buyers/3,160 sellers for the 4th edition)".
problem: The 822/533 and 1,028 figures are on the two cited pages. The 1,914 buyers/3,160 sellers figure is not on either cited page; it appears in Hinge's "Inside the Buyer's Brain" 2022 webinar deck (https://hingemarketing.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/IBB-Webinar-2022.pdf), which I opened and confirmed. The Hinge executive-summary page that would normally carry it returns HTTP 403.
fix: Add the webinar-PDF URL beside the 1,914/3,160 figure, or delete that figure from the resource entry.

problem: The page is undated and carries no publication year. The interview references "last month, in January" and "right now in February", which is consistent with either 2025 or 2026, so the 2025 label is unsupported as stated.
fix: Mark the year as "undated (interview references January/February, year not stated)" rather than 2025.

claim: Strength ratings are internally inconsistent across vendor sources: finding 6 (Belkins/TNW cold-email benchmark) is "Medium" while finding 12 (Thryv vendor survey) is "Low".
problem: Both are vendor-published material. The Belkins benchmark is a large dataset (7.5M emails) but is delivered as a Belkins-authored op-ed on a news site, i.e. vendor marketing with a self-reported methodology; the brief gives no reason for treating it as stronger than the other vendor source.
fix: Either rate finding 6 "Low-Medium" with a note that the dataset is large but self-reported by a lead-gen vendor with no independent audit, or explain in the evidence line why the sample size lifts it above Thryv.
